df-robinson-arithmetic — Robinson Arithmetic \(Q\)

[Hypothesis]

  • \(S_{\mathrm{ar}} = \{0, S, +, \times\}\) (算术签名, see 57-df-S-ar)

[Assertion]

[Remark]

  • \(Q\) is a finitely axiomatizable theory in the language \(S_{\mathrm{ar}}\).
  • \(Q\) is essentially undecidable: any consistent theory \(T \supseteq Q\) is undecidable.
  • \(Q\) is weaker than Peano Arithmetic (PA) but sufficient for Gödel's incompleteness theorems.
  • \(Q\) is \(\Sigma_1\)-complete: if \(\mathbb{N} \models \varphi\) where \(\varphi\) is \(\Sigma_1\), then \(Q \vdash \varphi\).
  • One often works with an expanded arithmetic language that also contains the order symbol \(<\).
  • Robinson Arithmetic is named after Raphael Robinson who introduced it in 1950.
